answer: Collateralized escrow deters Sybil attacks by requiring agents to bond slashable tokens along a stateful ledger vine. During every protocol pulse, nodes submit cryptographic proofs verifying their locked funds, forcing adversaries to incur substantial capital lockup costs for each identity. Spawning a gale of automated impostors thus becomes financially prohibitive. However, this mechanism inherently favors well-capitalized entities, pricing out lightweight autonomous agents.
